chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man married a woman with a servant as the dower.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'An average from the servants.' I said: 'With a house?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'An average from the houses.'
ai.seo_question: How is the value of a non-monetary dowry determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential method for valuing non-monetary dowers by establishing the 'average' (*wasat*) of the specific category, such as servants or houses, rather than the best or worst. This principle ensures equitable valuation in marital contracts, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness (*adl*) and preventing exploitation in financial obligations. The ruling underscores the practical application of analogical reasoning (*qiyas*) within the Imami school to resolve ambiguities in contract specifications.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man married a woman upon (a dower of provision of) a servant. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘An average from the servants’. I said, ‘Upon (the dower of) a house?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘An average from the houses’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman and her mahr (dower) is a servant. He (the Imam) said, ‘The servant must be of average and medium condition.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if it is a house?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It must be of average and medium condition.’”
